query: Which module declares the full set of settings a caller can pass when constructing the job runner and when submitting a job: parallelism limit, auto-begin, jobs-per-window cap and window length, carrying unfinished work into the next window, per-job deadline, ordering weight, job identifier, and cancellation handle?
why: The file is nothing but the documented option type declarations: TimeoutOptions (L3-25), constructor Options with concurrency/autoStart/queueClass/intervalCap/interval/carryoverIntervalCount/strict (L27-95), QueueAddOptions with priority/id (L97-109), TaskOptions with the AbortSignal (L111-148). index.ts consumes these but does not define them.

query: Which module is the built-in storage for waiting jobs that keeps them sorted by importance, preserves arrival order among equal importance, and leaves already-taken entries at the front until it periodically compacts them away?
why: The whole class is that store: compactionThreshold and #head cursor (L5-15), enqueue with FIFO append for equal/lower weight and binary insertion otherwise (L17-48), setPriority/remove/filter skipping the consumed prefix (L50-113), dequeue with reset/compaction (L82-100), #compact (L119-127). queue.ts is only the interface; lower-bound.ts is only the binary-search helper.

query: Where are the tests for the throttling mode that uses a rolling time window instead of fixed resetting windows, so bursts can never occur at window boundaries, including how it interacts with cancellation, pausing, clearing and concurrency limits?
why: Every test in the file constructs the queue with strict: true: sliding-window assertion helper (L6-13), enforces sliding window (L15-36), vs fixed window (L38-92), clear/pause/AbortSignal/concurrency/boundary-burst cases (L116-834). No other test file sets strict: true; advanced.ts and rate-limit.ts only cover fixed-window throttling and its events.

query: Where are the tests for inspecting the runner's live internal state: the list of jobs executing right now with their remaining deadline time, whether it is at full capacity with work waiting, and whether deadline errors report the runner's state?
why: runningTasks tests including timeoutRemaining (L6-229), isSaturated tests for concurrency, paused and throttled queues (L231-288), and timeout error message containing queue state (L290-324). runningTasks and timeoutRemaining appear in no other test file; strict.ts has only a single isSaturated case.

query: Which script measures the throughput of the job runner across scenarios like no ordering weights, random weights, steadily increasing weights, a large backlog started at once, and draining the raw ordered store directly?
why: The file is a Benchmark.Suite (L1-32) registering baseline (L34-42), random priority (L44-54), increasing priority (L56-66), large-fifo-backlog (L68-77) and priority-queue-dequeue (L79-94) runs and printing the fastest (L96-106). No other indexed file uses the benchmark library or measures timing throughput.

query: Which module is the actual queue engine — the class that enforces a concurrency ceiling, tracks fixed-window and sliding-window throttling internally, wires up cancellation via abort signals, and emits every lifecycle event, exposing the methods callers use to add work, pause/resume, inspect what's running, and wait on various completion signals?
why: The whole file is the PQueue class: constructor validation (L100-134), private interval/rate-limit bookkeeping (L137-372), concurrency and priority control (L382-438), add/addAll with abort-signal wiring (L440-604), lifecycle methods start/pause/clear (L595-645), the onEmpty/onSizeLessThan/onIdle/onPendingZero/onRateLimit/onRateLimitCleared/onError wait-promise family (L652-780), and the size/pending/isPaused/isRateLimited/isSaturated/runningTasks getters (L785-966). priority-queue.ts is only the default backing store and queue.ts is only its interface.

query: Which file declares the minimal contract — a size reading, inserting work, taking the next item, filtering by criteria, and reprioritizing by id — that any custom backing store must satisfy to be swapped in for the built-in one?
why: The file is nothing but the Queue<Element, Options> type: size, filter, dequeue, enqueue, setPriority and an optional remove (L3-11), plus the RunFunction alias (L1). priority-queue.ts implements this contract but is the concrete store, not the contract itself; options.ts references queueClass but does not define what it must implement.

query: Where are the tests for the default (non-strict) queue's everyday behavior — running jobs under a concurrency ceiling, ordering by importance, per-job and queue-wide deadlines, the different empty/idle/pending-zero completion signals, clearing, batch submission, constructor input checks, and fixed-window throttling timings?
why: test/basic.ts is the core suite: add() under varying concurrency and priority (L14-133), timeout behavior (L135-222), onEmpty/onIdle/onSizeLessThan/onPendingZero in many states (L224-573), clear() (L575-649), addAll() (L651-692), constructor/property validation (L694-809), autoStart/pause/start (L811-885), mixed sync/async and error handling (L887-939), fixed-window throttling timing scenarios (L986-1222), and onError() (L1224-1344). Cancellation, event-emission and sliding-window scenarios live in advanced.ts and strict.ts instead.

query: Where are the tests confirming every lifecycle event fires at the right moment, that cancelling a queued or running job through an abort signal cleans up its listeners and frees whatever slot or rate-limit accounting it held, and that interval timing carries over correctly across idle periods and rapid state changes?
why: test/advanced.ts covers: clearing the interval timer on pause (L9-24), each lifecycle event — active/idle/empty/add/next/completed/error (L26-263), abort-signal cancellation including custom reasons, paused queues, duplicate/explicit ids, and listener cleanup (L287-800), pending-count timing (L802-850), interval carryover and reset across idle periods (L852-1103), setPriority reordering under different concurrency levels (L934-1243), and rate-limit event/state edge cases including microtask batching and dynamic concurrency changes (L1296-1948). No other test file exercises abort-signal listener cleanup or the full lifecycle-event set.

query: Which file's only job is a compile-time check — confirming the TypeScript type checker infers the correctly-typed promise from submitting a job, without executing anything at runtime?
why: test-d/index.test-d.ts (L1-6) uses tsd's expectType to assert queue.add(async () => 'unicorn') is typed Promise<string>. It is the sole type-level test file; every other test/*.ts file runs assertions at runtime via node:test.
